Okay, long answer incoming.

What are Native Americans? What are Jews? What are Africans? How many ancestors, what percentage of DNA, etc etc etc?

The thing about race is - the edges of it are fuzzy, and there aren't strict and clear boundaries that everyone agrees on. This seems to be a common talking point for people who want to discredit the concept of race, but it misses something obvious. To illustrate this obvious something, let me provide some analogous questions:

  • What is the difference between a puddle and a lake? Seems like an obvious question on its face. But what is the exact difference in liters? At what point does a large puddle, if you add one more drop of water, become a lake?

  • How do you exactly define a breed of dog? They all descend from the same line of wolves, essentially... so, how many generations apart do two breeds have to be before they are different breeds? If a dalmation is cross-bred with a beagle, how many generations of breeding with dalmations must their offspring do before we call their descendants dalmations again? If a dalmation/beagle hybrid has spots like a dalmation, is it a dalmation, or is it a mixed breed?

Yet, there clearly is a difference between a pond and a lake, isn't there? Beagles and dalmations and cockerspaniels and rottweilers are all clearly different breeds, and their functional differences go dramatically beyond appearance, no?

The overwhelmingly vast majority of humans clearly fall into distinct racial categories. People will argue on how to exactly define the boundaries of these groups. Skin color and facial features are a quick and dirty shortcut to recognizing this through generalizations, because it can be fairly accurate for its ease of distinction, but that's not really what its about.

There are genetic haplogroups wherein different populations of humans can be split along where they cluster, and they are pretty clearly defined as separate from other groups and more closely related to those within their groups. This is indicative of having split off from another race long ago enough to have evolved into their own clearly separate group. But it is not purely a matter of having different random genetic information. These differences in gene mutations are generally reflective of the fact that these different groups, once split off, had to migrate to new environments and form new social structures and lifestyles adapted to those environments - thus putting different natural and sexual selection pressures on the populations. These created different peoples, with different qualities. It is born out by any number of facts, be it statistically relevant differences in average IQs even when normalizing for social factors, or tendency for groups to support individual rights versus collectivism (even when raised in a culture with views opposing their own), and many other measurable effects.

We are adapted to our historical environments, and the people who have historically been around us. Those who are most genetically similar, generally speaking, had to adapt to similar physical environments, and to the groups around us (who were most likely to be other groups closely related to us), thus forming the most compatible societies over a long history. Those who are genetically adapted to the same environments, and genetically predisposed toward success in the same types of societies, effectively form a single people in some sense. Of course they can be broken up into further distinctions, but a native German and a native Swede will functionally be the same people in a way that a native German and a light-skinned native Iranian or Korean simply won't be. And if the Germans all mate with a very culturally and genetically distinct people, like Somalis, they may form what might be considered one race... but it will be distinct in form and function from both German and Somali people. And they will build a different society than either the Germans or the Somalians, with different values and average capacities and so on, than either the Germans or the Somalis.

So, what is the "white race"? To me, the white race refers generally to the descendants of the Indo-European peoples, without significant admixture from other groups (unlike the northern Indian or the Iranian descendants of Indo-European peoples), who have a history in the long interconnected societies in the general area we now call "Europe". You can generally recognize them by their light skin and traditionally "European" facial features, though that is more of a rule of thumb than an exact definition. Though their different groups, living separately, have often warred with each other, they have shown that members of one group are easily integrated into the societies of another - so much so that the initial immigrants often do not have to vastly change their values and lifestyles (if they are moving into the same social class of the host nation), and their first or second generation descendants are both likely to see themselves and be seen as part of the native in-group. Not everyone will agree with my exact definition, but most people will have zero disagreement with me on the vast majority of white people (or Africans, or Asians, etc etc.). Essentially nobody will mistake a native Brit and a native Pakistani for both being the same race of people.

I do not count Jews among whites, even though the Ashkinazim frequently have a significant amount of Eastern European DNA, and often have very light skin. Why? They also tend to have a significant amount of genetic admixture from Semetic populations, and have kept themselves separate (in terms of breeding) from the general European population for as many generations as they can - instead adapting to their own insular (and very distinct) social structures and values and sexual selection strategies. They are functionally a separate people, basically their own race. It is much how the Hispanics are mostly Mestizos - a mixture of Spanish and native American genetics - but function as their own distinct race, both genetically and socially different from both Europeans and native Americans in clearly identifiable ways. The Jews have been a largely separate people for far longer than the Hispanic Mestizos have been.

Do mixed Europeans count as white? That's an interesting question. I can't give you an exact percentage of white European blood a person must hold before he is counted as "white". Luckily, the percentage of highly mixed people is still so small that it's not really a major issue to be resolved yet. Though I do not have an exact percentage that everyone would agree on, I do have a couple of stories about Indians and White people that might give people something to think about on this topic.

I suppose there are a variety of ways that the relationships between populations and borders could work. My main goal would be for all people who view themselves as a single people to have a single polity in which they are the overwhelming majority, so as to be able to run it in their own interests. Everybody has a "home" to do with as they please, so to speak.

Ideally, I'd keep much of the world's borders as they are - considering much of the nations of the world are relatively homogeneous as it is. There are some places where I would not change the borders, but I would return some of the recent immigrants to their homelands if their numbers are starting to swell and cause conflicts. I'd make the Native American reservations more autonomous, and perhaps expand some of them to include enough land and resources to truly be autonomous, really functioning as their own countries. I'd remove all the Jewish communities in America (as well as everywhere else but Israel, really) and put them in Israel, since they tend to stay insular and hold separate interests from non-Jewish host nations, yet retain a lot of common identity and interests with themselves internationally. Now that I think about it, some very ethnically distinct Jews (like the Ethiopian Jews) really are treated as different from the majority of Jews, so perhaps they'd just need their own separate nations near where they are. Even though I'd keep places in Europe like Germany and France separate, since they function as different nations, I wouldn't separate different European descended peoples in America since they seem to effectively function as one people. I would probably split the East and West coasts off into their own nations though, since they are so culturally and politically different from the central United States.

There are a number of lands I'd do this to. China is another good example, having a number of areas that are comprised of different ethnicities and cultures that are dominated by the Han.
